evidence.notes: PaymentClient::transfer became private and the old free execute_transfer was deleted; PaymentGateway owns the client and a Guard built from one trusted issuer PublicKey with zero clock tolerance. execute_transfer builds a ReceivedAuthorization from the presented chain and PoP signature only, calls Guard::guard_received on the same recipient/amount it then executes with, and maps denials to PaymentError. Unlike the 2026-09-17 baseline, every denial is proven at the boundary: forged wrong-holder proofs, untrusted issuers, expired and wrong-capability warrants, and constraint violations are submitted directly to the gateway and assert transfer_count() == 0; the wider child is rejected at attenuation and the unwidened parent still runs once. The run followed the new native-tools routing (ran scripts/inspect_native_tools.py). Weaknesses: bypass absence rests on the symbol being removed rather than an attempted call such as a compile_fail doctest, and the report omits the trust-levels label the skill now requires, though it names the missing external issuer and disclaims replay, receipts, and revocation distribution.
